---
title: Add a node kind to the browser runner
description: "Adding a screen for a new element type, so a schema type runs rather than only drawing."
---

| Folder in `packages/runner/src/nodes/` | Claims | What the participant sees |
|---|---|---|
| `start/` | `bpmn:StartEvent` | The consent form, or a welcome with a *Begin* button |
| `end/` | `bpmn:EndEvent` | The completion code and the redirect countdown |
| `instruction/` | `cognitive:Instruction` | The `content` text and a *Continue* button |
| `questionnaire/` | `cognitive:Questionnaire` | A built-in item set, or a free-text box |
| `behaverse/` | `cognitive:BehaverseTask` | The Behaverse Unity build in a frame |
| `choreography/` | `bpmn:ChoreographyTask` | The two participants and which one initiates |
| `task/` | Any task no folder above claimed | The step's name, any declared call, and *Continue* |

[Execution](../run/execution.qmd) sets that list beside the other three programs.

## Drawable is not runnable

| Declaring a type in a schema gives it | It does not give it |
|---|---|
| A palette entry and an icon | A screen in the browser runner |
| Inspector fields for its attributes | A job the session can hand to a component |
| Round-tripping through YAML, XML, and PNG | Any pre-flight check of the values an author typed |

An element the registry cannot match warns twice and is stepped past: once before the run, from the pre-flight in `packages/runner/src/nodes/index.ts`, and once as the token reaches it, from `packages/runner/src/session.ts`. Gateways need no folder — the session picks their branch itself rather than dispatching to a screen, so the walk never reports them as unrunnable.

::: {.callout-note}
Two things a schema *can* say change the run with no node module: an applied type whose branching is `random` is drawn from the seeded generator, and one whose branching is `model` stops the run rather than guessing. Both live in [Execution](../run/execution.qmd#how-a-branch-is-chosen).
:::

## One folder, discovered at startup

A node kind is one directory, `packages/runner/src/nodes/<kind>/`. Nothing registers it by hand: `packages/runner/src/nodes/index.ts` runs

```ts
import.meta.glob('./*/index.tsx', { eager: true });
```

so every `<kind>/index.tsx` is imported at startup and self-registers as a side effect. The mutable array and `registerNode` live in `registry.ts`, apart from that glob, so a node module can import the one without re-triggering the other -- the circular import that would otherwise bite.

Keep React in `index.tsx`; attribute reading, payload building, and validators go in a plain `.ts` file beside it, where they stay testable in Node without a browser.

## The definition

`instruction/` is the smallest shipped kind, and its registration is the whole contract:

```tsx
registerNode({
  type: 'instruction',
  match: { extensionType: 'cognitive:Instruction' },
  toJob: (node) => ({ type: 'instruction', node, content: readString(node, 'content') ?? '' }),
  Component: Instruction,
  validateNode: validateInstruction,
});
```

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `type` | The kind's name, unique across the registry. Registering a duplicate throws at startup rather than shadowing silently. |
| `match` | Which elements this kind claims. Three shapes, below. |
| `toJob` | Maps a flow node to a plain job object -- the node plus whatever the component needs, read off the business object here rather than in the component. Return `null` and the step is logged and skipped. |
| `Component` | The React component shown while the token sits on this node. |
| `validateNode` | Optional. Runs once per node this kind matched, before the run starts. |
| `validateStudyflow` | Optional. Runs once per studyflow, for checks that span nodes this kind does *not* match. Only `task/` needs it, to check `implementation` references wherever they appear. |

Each module makes its job type visible to the session with a `declare module` block augmenting the runner's job map -- no shared file to edit.

## How an element finds its kind

`packages/runner/src/nodes/registry.ts` resolves in a fixed order, most specific first.

| Matcher | Matches on | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `{ extensionType: 'cognitive:Instruction' }` | The element's applied type | Every domain kind |
| `{ bpmnType: 'bpmn:StartEvent' }`, or an array of them | The BPMN type | `start/`, `end/`, `choreography/` |
| `{ fallback: 'task' }` | Any `bpmn:Task`, `bpmn:UserTask`, `bpmn:ServiceTask`, `bpmn:ScriptTask`, or `bpmn:ManualTask` left unclaimed | `task/`, and only `task/` |

Applied type beats BPMN type, so a `cognitive:Instruction` drawn on a `bpmn:Task` reaches `instruction/` and never the fallback. An element matching nothing is the warn-and-skip case above.

## What a component is given

Five props: its own typed `job`, the `session`, a `log` function, `complete()` to advance, and `abort(reason)` to stop the run with a message the participant sees.

`complete()` takes no result, on purpose -- nothing downstream reads one. Publish what the step collected with `session.setVariable(name, value)`: that is the value a condition on a sequence flow reads, and the value that goes to the data server with the session.

## Validation runs before the first screen

Both hooks return issues, and an issue's `severity` decides what happens to the run.

| `severity` | Effect |
|---|---|
| `error` (the default) | Blocks the run. The runner never shows a screen; it lists every problem with the id of its node under *This study cannot run*. |
| `warning` | Logged, and the run proceeds. Use it where the study is still deliverable but is not what the author probably meant -- an unknown questionnaire instrument, for instance, which downgrades to a free-text answer. |

Write the message as an instruction, not a diagnosis: the shipped validators name the attribute to fix and the value to put in it. The pre-flight entry point is async because kinds may fetch what they validate against -- today only `behaverse/`, checking scenes and timelines against the Unity build's manifest.

## Adding one, end to end

`cognitive:Rest` has no folder today, so a rest period falls through to the generic task screen. Giving it a real one is the whole exercise:

1. Create `packages/runner/src/nodes/rest/index.tsx`, declaring the job type and augmenting the job map there.
2. Read the attributes in `toJob`, render in the component, call `registerNode`.
3. Put anything that does not need React in a plain `.ts` file beside it.
4. Run any studyflow containing the element -- the glob picks the folder up.

```tsx
// packages/runner/src/nodes/rest/index.tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { readString, type FlowNode } from '@runner/flow';
import type { NodeProps } from '@runner/nodes/types';
import { NodePanel } from '@runner/nodes/NodePanel';
import { nodeStyles } from '@runner/nodes/styles';
import { registerNode } from '@runner/nodes/registry';
import { readDuration } from '@runner/nodes/rest/duration';

declare module '@runner/jobs' {
  interface JobsByType {
    rest: RestJob;
  }
}

type RestJob = { type: 'rest'; node: FlowNode; seconds: number };

function Rest({ job, complete }: NodeProps<RestJob>) {
  const [left, setLeft] = useState(job.seconds);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (left <= 0) {
      complete();
      return;
    }
    const id = window.setTimeout(() => setLeft((n) => n - 1), 1000);
    return () => window.clearTimeout(id);
  }, [left, complete]);

  return (
    <NodePanel>
      <h2 className={nodeStyles.title}>{job.node.businessObject?.name || 'Rest'}</h2>
      <p className={nodeStyles.subtitle}>Please wait. {left}s remaining.</p>
    </NodePanel>
  );
}

registerNode({
  type: 'rest',
  match: { extensionType: 'cognitive:Rest' },
  // `configurations` is YAML, so the parsing lives in a plain .ts file next door.
  toJob: (node) => ({ type: 'rest', node, seconds: readDuration(readString(node, 'configurations')) }),
  Component: Rest,
});
```

Because `cognitive:Rest` already ships in the cognitive schema, nothing else changes: the palette, the inspector, and the file format were never waiting on the runner.
